# Variables

Every environment variable the workspace's crates define, modules, packages and contracts alike, from their `variables.toml`, by the crate defining it, and each namespace a crate computes names in. A runtime flag may name one to read when it is absent, as its command's reference says, and a specification field never reads one.

## Defined

Each variable with its type, its default, and the crate defining it.

- `ALL_PROXY`, string, from `core`: This machine's proxy for every protocol, which Link hands the programs it installs and runs
- `AWS_RESPONSE_CHECKSUM_VALIDATION`, string, from `core`: When AWS's libraries check a response's checksum, which Link sets for rclone's run against a bucket that doesn't send one
- `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, string, from `core`: Set: colors even in a pipe or a file.
- `COLUMNS`, string, from `core`: Your terminal's width, where Link can't ask the terminal.
- `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, string, from `core`: Your desktop's bus, which a sandbox opens only when its specification grants the desktop.
- `DISPLAY`, string, from `core`: Your X11 desktop, which a sandbox opens only when its specification grants the desktop.
- `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT`, string, from `core`: Whether git may ask in a terminal for a credential: `0` keeps it from asking, as Link sets it for a git it runs alone.
- `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, string, from `core`: The key file a program using Google Cloud's libraries signs in with, which Link passes on only to a cloud's own run
- `HOME`, string, from `core`: Must be absolute, or commands that delete or trust a folder refuse.
- `HOSTNAME`, string, from `core`: This machine's name, where the system doesn't give one: scrubbed from reports.
- `HTTPS_PROXY`, string, from `core`: This machine's HTTPS proxy, which Link hands the programs it installs and runs
- `HTTP_PROXY`, string, from `core`: This machine's HTTP proxy, which Link hands the programs it installs and runs
- `LANG`, string, from `core`: Your locale, kept for programs Link runs.
- `LNK_CORE`, string, from `core`: A core program a test runs in place of the one built beside it, for tests
- `LNK_EXE`, string, from `core`: The `lnk` that started a module, which it runs for other commands.
- `LNK_GITHUB_URL`, string, from `core`: Where a module from outside Link is read from in place of `https://github.com` (tests): a location of the kinds `LNK_RELEASES_URL` takes, holding each repository's releases at `<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest/download`. Its pinned key is still checked.
- `LNK_INSECURE`, string, from `core`: `1`: install without `ssh-keygen`, so without checking the signature.
- `LNK_INSTALLATION_DIR`, string, from `core`: This installation's folder [default: `~/.lnk`], for one process and what it runs: a sandbox's session whose settings can't be in the folder it writes. A relative value is ignored.
- `LNK_INSTALL_DIR`, string, from `core`: Where `lnk` goes; modules go next to it.
- `LNK_MODULES`, string, from `core`: The module listing (`lnk module list --json`) `lnk` hands the module it runs, for that process alone, so its questions start no other `lnk`.
- `LNK_NO_BROWSER`, string, from `core`: Set to open no browser: a command that would open a page, such as `lnk issue create` or `lnk agent connect`, prints its address instead
- `LNK_RELEASES_URL`, string, from `core`: Where releases are read from (tests, staging and dev builds). Signatures remain required. An HTTPS address with no login, backslash, query or fragment, a bucket of yours (s3://<bucket>/<folder> or gs://<bucket>/<folder>, read with that cloud's CLI and your login) or a folder here (file:///<folder>); debug builds also accept HTTP on this machine.
- `LNK_TEST_RELEASE_SIGNERS`, string, from `core`: An allowed-signers file whose keys are trusted beside the built-in release signer (tests). Only debug builds read it.
- `LNK_UPDATE_NOTICE`, string, from `core`: `off`: commands never check for or announce a newer release.
- `LNK_VERSION`, string, from `core`: The release version to install, such as `0.0.1`. A released `lnk` refuses a version older than itself.
- `LOGNAME`, string, from `core`: Who you are, where `USER` isn't set: kept for programs Link runs, and scrubbed from reports.
- `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, string, from `core`: Certificates Node.js trusts besides its own
- `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY`, string, from `core`: Node.js's switch to send its requests through `HTTPS_PROXY`, set to 1 for a program Link runs in Node
- `NO_COLOR`, string, from `core`: Set: no colors. Colors show only on a terminal.
- `NO_PROXY`, string, from `core`: The hosts this machine reaches without its proxy
- `PATH`, string, from `core`: Where Link finds the programs it runs, and the modules beside `lnk`.
- `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, string, from `core`: Where Playwright keeps the browsers it installs
- `SHELL`, string, from `core`: Your shell, which a box opened here runs.
- `SSH_CONNECTION`, string, from `core`: Set over SSH: logins print their address instead of opening a browser.
- `SSH_TTY`, string, from `core`: Set over SSH: logins print their address instead of opening a browser.
- `SSL_CERT_FILE`, string, from `core`: The certificates this machine trusts, as OpenSSL and the programs built on it read them
- `TERM`, string, from `core`: Your terminal's kind, kept for programs Link runs.
- `TMPDIR`, string, from `core`: Where programs Link runs keep temporary files.
- `TZ`, string, from `core`: The time zone a program reports its times in
- `USER`, string, from `core`: Who you are: named in a box's or a service's unit, kept for programs Link runs, and scrubbed from reports.
- `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, string, from `core`: Your Wayland desktop, which a sandbox opens only when its specification grants the desktop.
- `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, string, from `core`: Your settings folder (Linux) [default: `~/.config`]: where services' units and programs' dot files are.
- `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, string, from `core`: Your runtime folder (Linux), where Link's sockets and services live.
- `all_proxy`, string, from `core`: `ALL_PROXY` as some programs spell it
- `http_proxy`, string, from `core`: `HTTP_PROXY` as some programs spell it
- `https_proxy`, string, from `core`: `HTTPS_PROXY` as some programs spell it
- `no_proxy`, string, from `core`: `NO_PROXY` as some programs spell it
- `npm_config_https_proxy`, string, from `core`: npm's HTTPS proxy
- `npm_config_noproxy`, string, from `core`: The hosts npm reaches without its proxy
- `LNK_ASKER_BUILT_FROM`, string, from `link-core`: The commit the program asking a question was built from, handed to the module answering it, which refuses the question when it was built from another.
- `LNK_BUILD`, string, from `link-core`: The build a program is compiled as: `dev`, `staging` or `prod`, set by `lnk bundle create` as it compiles a bundle's programs and read as each is compiled. Left out, a build from source.
- `LNK_COMPONENTS`, string, from `link-core`: Component folders outside `lnk`'s own workspace, joined as `PATH` is, whose modules a build of `lnk` lists, read as it's compiled. `lnk bundle create` sets it from the bundle's `components` and clears any other, so a bundle's `lnk` never depends on the shell or folder it was built from.
- `LNK_DEV_SIGNER`, string, from `link-core`: The allowed-signers line of the key a dev build is signed with, which `lnk bundle create --build dev` derives from your signer and a dev build reads as it's compiled, refusing to compile without it.
- `LNK_PROD_SIGNER`, string, from `link-core`: The allowed-signers line of the signer a prod build is signed with, which `lnk bundle` derives from the bundle's signer and a prod build reads as it's compiled, trusting it alone.
- `LNK_DISCORD_API`, string, from `discord`: Discord's HTTP API, for tests; the Gateway's address comes from it
- `LNK_DISCORD_TOKEN`, string, carries the secret `discord.bot_token`, from `discord`: The Discord bot's token, read by connect, which asks for it when it's unset
- `LNK_SIGNAL_CLI`, string, from `signal`: On Link Harness, a `signal-cli` of your own to carry Signal with, for tests; the account stays in `~/.lnk/safe/agents/<agent>/connections/signal`
- `LNK_SIGNAL_NUMBER`, string, from `signal`: The agent's Signal number, with its country code, not yours; connect asks for it when it's unset
- `LNK_SIGNAL_OWNER`, string, from `signal`: Your Signal number, with its country code, not the agent's; connect asks for it when it's unset
- `LNK_SLACK_API`, string, from `slack`: Slack's Web API, for tests
- `LNK_SLACK_APP_TOKEN`, string, carries the secret `slack.app_token`, from `slack`: The app-level token (xapp-...), with the bot token or neither, read by connect, which asks for it when it's unset
- `LNK_SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, string, carries the secret `slack.bot_token`, from `slack`: The bot token (xoxb-...), with the app token or neither, read by connect, which asks for it when it's unset
- `LNK_TELEGRAM_API`, string, from `telegram`: Telegram's Bot API, for tests
- `LNK_TELEGRAM_TOKEN`, string, carries the secret `telegram.bot_token`, from `telegram`: The bot token from BotFather, read by connect, which asks for it when it's unset; no flag takes a connection's token
- `LNK_MODEL_CREDENTIAL`, string, from `deepseek`: The model's key in dsh's .env, which its provider reads by name
- `npm_config_cache`, string, from `deepseek`: npm's cache folder, which a harness's install gives npm inside the harness's home, never the machine user's.
- `npm_config_update_notifier`, string, from `deepseek`: Whether npm checks for a newer npm: false in a harness's install, so npm never checks for its own updates.
- `HERMES_HOME`, string, from `hermes`: Where Hermes keeps its configuration and state: the agent's own folder, given to each Hermes process it runs.
- `LNK_HERMES_MANAGED_GATEWAY`, string, from `hermes`: Set to 1 in the Hermes gateway Link starts, so its workarounds know Link manages it
- `LNK_HERMES_MODEL_URL`, string, from `hermes`: The model's address in Hermes's `config.yaml`, reached through Link's proxy with the proxy's secret in it
- `LNK_OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN`, string, from `openclaw`: The OpenClaw gateway's token, kept in its .env and read back from it
- `LNK_OPENCLAW_MODEL_URL`, string, from `openclaw`: The model's address in an OpenClaw provider's entry, reached through Link's proxy with the proxy's secret in it
- `NODE_OPTIONS`, string, from `openclaw`: Node.js's options, which OpenClaw's gateway is started with, with Link's own added
- `OPENCLAW_HOME`, string, from `openclaw`: Where OpenClaw keeps its configuration and state, which OpenClaw's processes never inherit: Link names their folders itself.
- `LNK_*`, a namespace, from `aws`: CLI test overrides: append the uppercase program name (such as AWS) to `LNK_` when selecting the external AWS CLI.
- `LNK_*`, a namespace, from `gcp`: CLI test overrides: append the uppercase program name (such as GCLOUD or GSUTIL) to `LNK_` when selecting the external Google Cloud CLI.
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, string, from `agent`: The provider's own key variable, read by `lnk agent start`, `create`, `move` and `model set`: no flag takes a key. With no model yet, the one that is set (several set: refused, to unset all but one); with a hosted model, its provider's, to renew the key; with `--model`, the provider its name says; with a model on this computer, one that is set is asked about in a terminal (switch to that provider?), else said. Never passed to a harness or to a box.
- `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, string, from `agent`: Certificates curl trusts, which a harness's installer is given.
- `LNK_AGENT`, string, from `agent`: The agent's name, for harness programs.
- `LNK_AGENT_FOLDER`, string, from `agent`: The agent's own folder (`~/Link/Agents/<name>/agent`), for a harness that keeps Link's collections (Link Harness): each one kept at `file` a folder of it.
- `LNK_AGENT_ID`, string, from `agent`: The agent's ID, for harness programs.
- `LNK_AGENT_SERVICE`, string, from `agent`: The service the agent acts as, its bare ID, for harness programs: what its bridge calls prove beside its ID.
- `LNK_FALLBACK_CREDENTIAL`, string, from `agent`: The fallback's key on `lnk agent start --model.fallback_model`, read before its provider's own variable.
- `LNK_FILES`, string, from `agent`: The agent's Home, its files folder, for harness programs.
- `LNK_MEASURES`, string, from `agent`: For harness programs: the file in the harness's home it may append its own measures to, as OTLP (`.lnk/safe/measures/measures.jsonl`), which `lnk measure` reads.
- `LNK_OWNER`, string, from `agent`: The agent's owner, for harness programs.
- `LNK_PORT`, string, from `agent`: The agent's base port, for harness programs: every agent's own.
- `LNK_TEST_BRIDGE_NONE_FOR_MS`, string, from `agent`: Debug builds only: milliseconds an empty shared bridge waits before it stops.
- `LNK_TEST_MIGRATE_STOP`, string, from `agent`: Debug builds only: stop migration before this numbered step so recovery can be tested.
- `OPENAI_API_KEY`, string, from `agent`: The provider's own key variable, read by `lnk agent start`, `create`, `move` and `model set`: no flag takes a key. With no model yet, the one that is set (several set: refused, to unset all but one); with a hosted model, its provider's, to renew the key; with `--model`, the provider its name says; with a model on this computer, one that is set is asked about in a terminal (switch to that provider?), else said. Never passed to a harness or to a box.
- `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, string, from `agent`: The provider's own key variable, read by `lnk agent start`, `create`, `move` and `model set`: no flag takes a key. With no model yet, the one that is set (several set: refused, to unset all but one); with a hosted model, its provider's, to renew the key; with `--model`, the provider its name says; with a model on this computer, one that is set is asked about in a terminal (switch to that provider?), else said. Never passed to a harness or to a box.
- `PIP_CERT`, string, from `agent`: Certificates pip trusts, which a harness's installer is given.
- `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, string, from `agent`: Certificates Python's requests trusts, which a harness's installer is given.
- `LNK_*`, a namespace, from `agent`: Link's own variables, none holding a secret, forwarded whole to the agent's background bridges and its owner's shared harness service.
- `LNK_CODE`, string, from `harness-contract`: The code tool's address in a harness's environment: its project's language servers, each in a sandbox
- `LNK_FILE`, string, from `harness-contract`: The file tool's address in a harness's environment: its files read and written as its sandbox file says
- `LNK_RUN`, string, from `harness-contract`: The run tool's address in a harness's environment: its commands, each in a sandbox of its own
- `LNK_MODEL_URL`, string, from `model`: The calling agent's granted model namespace, which the typed model commands call when it's set
- `LNK_FALLBACK_MODEL_URL`, string, from `link-model-contract`: The fallback model's namespace, handed to a sandbox whose grant has one, beside `LNK_MODEL_URL`
- `LNK_STORE_AGENT`, string, from `store`: Storage driver protocol: the agent the storage bridge selected for the request being served
- `LNK_STORE_DIR`, string, from `store`: Storage driver protocol: the absolute folder holding the agent collections the storage bridge asks the driver to serve
- `CHROMIUM`, string, from `browser-tool`: The Chromium the browser's tests drive, ahead of one on PATH or Playwright's
- `LNK_TEST_NOTES_PARENT`, string, from `memory-tool`: A folder the notes test, on a Mac, saves beneath where memory's sandbox can't read it; the test runs only when it's set
- `LNK_MEMORY`, string, from `memory`: The agent's memory's address in its harness's environment: an MCP server over HTTP
- `LNK_MEMORY_DRIVER`, string, from `memory`: The store driver the agent's specification keeps its conversations by, the only one memory runs to read them; unset, it runs none
- `LNK_MEMORY_FROM`, boolean, from `memory`: 1 when the agent's harness is sent messages from others, so memory writes notes only in the owner's conversations
- `LNK_MEMORY_MODEL`, string, from `memory`: The address of the embedding model memory ranks by, an OpenAI-style API on this machine; empty when no runtime here has the model
- `LNK_MEMORY_NOTES`, string, from `memory`: The agent's notes file memory may write; unset, it writes nothing of the agent's folder
- `LNK_MEMORY_SPEC`, string, from `memory`: The agent's [tool.memory] opinions as JSON, in the environment of every memory command; unset, the engine's own
- `LNK_RUN_CONTEXT`, string, from `link-run-tool-contract`: The run server's protected context, its named routes and the agent's binding lookup, read outside every task's sandbox and never passed to a task
- `LNK_CRONTAB`, string, from `scheduler-tool`: A program to stand in for crontab in tests: the scheduler's cron driver writes its line through it, on a Mac too
- `LNK_TEST_SCHEDULER_WAKE`, string, from `scheduler-tool`: Set by the runner's test of a wake beside another runner's firing, to run that test alone in a child of its own
- `BRAVE_API_KEY`, string, from `web-tool`: Your Brave Search API key, in web's environment, never the harness's
- `LNK_WEB_SEARCH`, string, from `web-tool`: The search API web uses when both keys are set: brave or tavily
- `LNK_WEB_SEARCH_URL`, string, from `web-tool`: Where search requests go instead of the provider's API, for tests: read only by a debug build, https or http to loopback
- `TAVILY_API_KEY`, string, from `web-tool`: Your Tavily API key, in web's environment, never the harness's
- `LNK_RESOURCE_JOURNAL`, string, from `cloud-contract`: Private JSONL file for durable machine launch intents and sibling disposable-job identity records; unset disables journaling.
- `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`, string, from `box`: Read once by `lnk cloud connect aws`: the login to reuse and its region.
- `AWS_PROFILE`, string, from `box`: Read once by `lnk cloud connect aws`: the login to reuse and its region.
- `AWS_REGION`, string, from `box`: Read once by `lnk cloud connect aws`: the login to reuse and its region.
- `CLOUDSDK_CONFIG`, string, from `box`: gcloud's own settings, as gcloud reads them: `lnk cloud connect gcp` asks gcloud where its login is.
- `LNK_AWS`, string, from `box`: The cloud CLIs the adapters run (tests).
- `LNK_BOX`, string, from `box`: In a setup script's environment: the box it sets up.
- `LNK_BOX_HERE`, string, from `box`: In what `lnk box run` and `lnk box ssh` run in a box here: the box's name. `lnk box user` refuses there, since a box user is a login on a machine of its own.
- `LNK_BOX_SSH`, string, from `box`: How `lnk box` reaches a box: `direct`, its port 22; `tunnel`, through its cloud's own tunnel over HTTPS (AWS Systems Manager, Google Cloud's IAP), where port 22 can't be reached, as from a network that allows only HTTPS. A tunnel to a box on AWS needs AWS's `session-manager-plugin` here. Anything else fails, saying so.
- `LNK_GCLOUD`, string, from `box`: The cloud CLIs the adapters run (tests).
- `LNK_SSH`, string, from `box`: What `lnk box` runs (tests).
- `LNK_SSH_KEYGEN`, string, from `box`: What `lnk box` runs (tests).
- `LNK_TEST_BOX_END`, string, from `box`: Debug builds only: read the disposable-box ending policy from this file instead of `/etc/lnk/end.json`.
- `LNK_*`, a namespace, from `box`: SSH program overrides: append the uppercase program name with dashes changed to underscores, such as `LNK_SSH` or `LNK_SSH_KEYGEN`.
- `LNK_JOB_OUT`, string, from `env`: In a job's environment: the folder whose files go to its bucket with `--out`.
- `LNK_SUDO`, string, from `env`: What runs a root stage, service or job on a box, for tests. A debug build reads it; a release build doesn't.
- `LNK_TEST_BOX_ROOT`, string, from `env`: A folder standing for `/` where `lnk box user` keeps a box's users and their programs, owned by the user rather than root, for tests of a stand-in box. A debug build reads it; a release build doesn't.
- `LNK_TEST_JOB_GROUP`, string, from `env`: Debug builds only: sample this process group instead of the current job process tree.
- `LNK_TEST_KEEPER`, string, from `env`: The socket of a keeper of your secrets that a test serves, used in place of `/run/lnk-secrets/keeper.sock` whether or not this machine has the `lnk-secrets` user. A debug build reads it; a release build doesn't.
- `LNK_TEST_MACHINE_KIND`, string, from `env`: A file read in place of `/etc/lnk/kind.toml`, owned by the user rather than root, for tests of a stand-in box. A debug build reads it; a release build doesn't.
- `LNK_TEST_WORKERS_SETTINGS`, string, from `env`: A trusted worker settings file for a test's stand-in box, owned by the current user or root. A debug build reads it; a release build doesn't.
- `DEBIAN_FRONTEND`, string, from `sandbox`: How Debian's installer asks: `noninteractive` as the sandbox installs bubblewrap with apt on a box, where no one answers, so nothing waits on a question.
- `LNK_CHECK_SECRET`, string, from `sandbox`: The bait secret `lnk sandbox check` gives a helper it starts outside the sandbox, in its environment, for the probe that tries to read another program's environment: never a real secret.
- `LNK_PROBE_*`, string, from `sandbox`: What `lnk sandbox check` hands each probe it runs inside the sandbox: its bait and what it tries (`LNK_PROBE_ARG`), the folders it reads or writes, the ports and machines it reaches. Its `*`: What the probe is handed, as `ARG` or `CANARY`.
- `LNK_SANDBOX_CALLER`, string, from `sandbox`: The sandbox a tool's server serves, which the bridge sets as it starts the server for that sandbox's session: a namespace asks and pauses as its caller, and serves no sandbox without it.
- `LNK_SANDBOX_LEARN_FD`, string, from `sandbox`: Into the sandbox, for its first program, which removes it: the descriptor it writes each program started to. A program inside that sets it only records what it runs itself.
- `LNK_TEST_CA`, string, from `sandbox`: A certificate authority's PEM file the sandbox's proxy trusts beside this machine's, for a test's own host over TLS. A debug build reads it; a release build doesn't.
- `LNK_TEST_ON_CLOUD`, string, from `sandbox`: `1`: the sandbox takes this machine for a cloud's, refusing `[lan]` what it refuses there (tests). Nothing makes a cloud's machine not one.
- `LNK_TEST_RESOLVE`, string, from `sandbox`: `name=address`, comma separated: the sandbox's proxy gives each name those addresses without asking this machine's resolver (tests, on a machine without DNS). A debug build reads it; a release build doesn't.
- `SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`, string, from `sandbox`: The command an SSH client asked for, which `lnk sandbox enter`, a key's forced command, runs in the sandbox.
- `LD_AUDIT`, string, from `link-sandbox-confine`: Libraries the system's dynamic loader hands every symbol a program binds: never inherited by a confined program.
- `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, string, from `link-sandbox-confine`: Folders the system's dynamic loader searches for a program's libraries before its own: never inherited by a confined program.
- `LD_PRELOAD`, string, from `link-sandbox-confine`: Libraries the system's dynamic loader loads into every program first, which a confined program never inherits, and `lnk sandbox check` sets to prove a loaded library stays inside the sandbox too.
- `LNK_PROXY_LISTENER_FD`, string, from `sandbox-client`: Proxy startup protocol: inherited TCP listener descriptor, validated against the requested loopback address before use.
- `LNK_SANDBOX_OPEN`, string, from `sandbox-client`: Sandbox browser protocol: authenticated loopback proxy URL used by the browser-opening shim.
- `LNK_TEST_BOOTSTRAP`, string, from `secret`: Debug builds only: permit the bootstrap test launcher to receive box credentials without root.
- `LNK_TEST_TPM_DEVICE`, string, from `secret`: Debug builds only: TPM device path used in place of `/dev/tpmrm0`.
- `LNK_TEST_TPM`, string, from `link-secret-contract`: Debug builds only: substitute the TPM tool for isolated secret-storage tests.
- `LNK_TEST_TPM_RUN`, string, from `link-secret-contract`: Debug builds only: private operation folder used by isolated TPM tests.
- `LNK_PERSONAL_DIR`, string, from `storage`: Your files folder, an absolute path.
- `LNK_RCLONE`, string, from `storage`: Run this rclone instead, unchecked (tests).
- `AWS_*`, a namespace, from `storage`: AWS's sign-in variables, removed from a run that signs in as a cloud's own account
- `RCLONE_*`, a namespace, from `storage`: rclone's own settings, each removed from its run so only Link's settings file sets it up
- `LNK_ARTIFACT_BUDGET`, string, from `link-artifact`: Positive byte budget for the shared immutable-download cache; defaults to 2147483648 bytes.
- `LNK_ARTIFACT_CACHE`, string, from `link-artifact`: Shared folder for verified immutable downloads; defaults to this machine's cache/artifacts folder.
- `CARGO`, string, from `link-component`: The Cargo that builds a component's programs for its tests [default: cargo].
- `LNK_BUILT_FROM`, string, from `link-component`: The commit a release build from source was built from, which a component's build script gives each program as it's compiled (`link_component::SOURCE_VARIABLE`), so a question names the commit its asker was built from.
- `LNK_DESCRIPTION_PROTOCOL`, string, from `link-component`: The description protocol version of the program asking another for its description or `lnk` for its registry (`link_component::PROTOCOL_VARIABLE`). The answerer answers in it, and refuses one below the oldest it accepts, naming the upgrade.
- `LNK_EXEC_DIR`, string, from `link-files`: Absolute adapter program directory, staged during install and read only during a run. It grants no filesystem access.
- `LNK_UPGRADE_PROTOCOL`, string, from `link-files`: The upgrade protocol version of the core asking a program of a release what it changes, or to make its changes (`link_files::upgrade::PROTOCOL_VARIABLE`): the program answers in that version, and refuses one below the oldest it accepts, naming `lnk upgrade`. A program asked to write its files refuses an asker that states none.
- `LNK_INNER`, string, from `link-format`: Set for a nested Link command: leave next steps and the report footer to the outer command. An absolute folder is where it leaves its trace if it fails, for the outer report.
- `LNK_OUTPUT_COLOR`, string, from `link-format`: Output color setting: always, never or auto; aliases on/off and boolean spellings are accepted.
- `LNK_OUTPUT_EMPHASIS`, string, from `link-format`: Output emphasis setting: always, never or auto; aliases on/off and boolean spellings are accepted.
- `LNK_OUTPUT_LINKS`, string, from `link-format`: Output link setting: always, never or auto; aliases on/off and boolean spellings are accepted.
- `LNK_OUTPUT_SYMBOLS`, string, from `link-format`: Output symbols: emoji, plain or none; defaults to emoji.
- `RUST_LOG`, string, from `link-format`: What a service Link runs logs, as a Rust tracing filter such as `debug` [default: info]. The HTTP crates it calls through stay at warnings, as they log credentials below that.
- `LNK_INTERACTIONS`, string, from `link-interactions`: The machine's interaction store, an absolute folder, for a harness whose HOME is its own: lnk-agent names it where the harness reaches Link's settings, and the harness's tool calls then carry their work's binding.
- `LNK_SECURITY`, string, from `link-keychain`: Debug builds only: a Keychain tool stand-in for tests, which enables Keychain access on the test host; release builds always run `/usr/bin/security`.
- `LNK_SECRETS_FD`, string, from `link-secretive`: Private Link child-process protocol: descriptor for the sealed-off secret handoff pipe; never a credential value.
- `LNK_SECRET_DUMPABLE`, string, from `link-secretive`: Debug builds only: a nonempty value leaves process dumping enabled for a debugger or memory-isolation test.
- `LNK_SERVICES`, string, from `link-service`: Set to off to disable background service management.
- `LNK_TEST_SERVICE_SETTINGS`, string, from `link-service`: Debug builds only: select another service settings path while preserving root ownership, ancestor, mode and no-link trust checks.
- `LNK_HISTORY_PROTOCOL`, string, from `link-spec`: The history protocol version a program asking `lnk` for the release's history states: `lnk upgrade` asking the downloaded core, or a module its own core (`link_spec::history::PROTOCOL_VARIABLE`). The core answers in it, and refuses one below the oldest it accepts, naming the upgrade.
